transcript.content: Hello, welcome in. I'm Dr. Smith. To start off, can you tell me what brings you in to see me today?

Hey, Dr. Smith. Yeah, um, so I came in because I just feel like I’m literally crawling out of my skin whenever I’m supposed to sit still. Like, whether I'm working in the radiology suite or just sitting in a classroom for my college courses. 

Actually, speaking of the hospital, the cafeteria near the radiology department just completely changed their menu last week and they got rid of the spicy chicken sandwich. I used to get it literally every Tuesday. It's crazy how they just change things without asking anyone, you know? My buddy Mark was so mad he actually wrote a whole email to the hospital admin about it, which I told him was a waste of time, but he did it anyway. 

But, right, anyway—I've been trying to just tough it out for months now with the sitting still thing, but I just can't. I always end up pacing around, constantly shifting in my chair, or just finding some completely random excuse to get up and move. I just can't stay put.
Are you currently taking any prescription medications, especially any antipsychotics or anti-nausea drugs?

No, I'm not taking any prescriptions or anything like that. Definitely no antipsychotics or... what was the other one? Anti-nausea? Nah, I don't take anything for that. 

Although, honestly, I probably could have used some anti-nausea stuff a couple days ago because my buddy Mark—the guy who wrote that email about the sandwich—he's been getting really into making his own kombucha lately. Which is a terrible idea because his apartment is tiny and it just constantly smells like straight vinegar now. But he made me try this weird ginger-beet one he brewed in his closet, and man, my stomach was doing actual backflips all through my afternoon anatomy lecture. I literally had to just get up and leave halfway through. The professor was so annoyed because he's a massive stickler for attendance and always locks the door at exactly 2:05, but whatever, I couldn't just sit there. 

But yeah, to answer your question, no, no medications at all.
Do you also notice that you're frequently worrying excessively about different things—like work, school, or health—even when there's no clear reason to worry?

Worrying? Uh, no, not really. I don't really sit around stressing about stuff like that. Honestly, my mom is always telling me I probably need to worry *more* about things like school, but I just don't get anxious about it. 

Like with work, I don't stress. I mean, the radiology suite is usually pretty straightforward, except when the portable X-ray machine gets stuck. Oh man, last week the portable unit completely locked up on me while I was doing rounds up on the third floor. The wheels on those things are absolute garbage. I was trying to push it down the hallway and it kept pulling hard to the left, exactly like a shopping cart with a busted wheel. You know when you get that one bad cart at the grocery store and you just end up drifting into the cereal aisle the whole time? It drives me insane. I actually ended up just abandoning a cart at Target once because it was squeaking so loud everyone in the store was staring at me, and I was just trying to buy some new socks. 

But, uh... wait, what were we talking about? Oh, right, worrying. Yeah, no, I don't really do that. I just kind of go with the flow, you know?
Thinking back to when you were a kid, say before age 12, did you have this same kind of restlessness or trouble sitting still, like in elementary school?

Oh, yeah, 100 percent. My parents actually still talk about my elementary school parent-teacher conferences because it was always the exact same thing every year. The teachers would always complain that I was constantly out of my seat, just calling out answers, or rushing ahead on assignments before they even finished giving the directions. 

Like, my third-grade teacher, Mr. Henderson, he used to get so mad at me. He had this weird obsession with making everyone use these specific green gel pens for peer grading. Which, honestly, I hate gel pens. They always smear, especially if you're left-handed. My older sister is left-handed and she literally has to write with her hand hooked completely upside down so she doesn't drag it across the ink. She's actually studying to be an architect right now, which is wild to me because she used to just build these massive, completely structurally unsound forts out of our couch cushions when we were kids. One time she pulled down the entire living room curtain rod trying to make a roof for one of them, and my dad was furious because he had just patched the drywall there. Have you ever tried to clean up drywall dust? It gets everywhere. It's honestly worse than glitter. It gets into the carpet fibers and you just have to vacuum for like three days straight.

But, uh... wait, what were you asking? Oh, right, before age 12. Yeah, so all that stuff was happening way, way before middle school. It definitely isn't just something that started up recently since I began my radiology training or college classes.

final_diagnosis.reason: Patient reports pervasive, longstanding motor restlessness, inability to remain seated, fidgeting, and pacing across multiple settings (work, classroom). Collateral history from childhood (before age 12) confirms similar hyperactive-impulsive behaviors (out-of-seat behavior, blurting answers, rushing through tasks) noted by multiple teachers over several years, establishing early childhood onset and chronicity. Speech pattern shows marked tangentiality, distractibility, and difficulty maintaining focus on the interview topic, consistent with inattentive/impulsive cognitive style. Symptoms cause functional impairment in both academic and occupational settings. This pattern is most consistent with ADHD, predominantly hyperactive-impulsive presentation.
